title: Fundamental classes before absolute purity for regular schemes over a trait
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, put $A=\mathbf F_\ell$, and work on ordinary small-etale $D^+$ with signed Tate twists and ordinary compact-support right adjoints $p^!$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist, thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. A trait is $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$, where $R$ is a Noetherian local domain of dimension one with principal maximal ideal. Suppose $S$ is complete and strictly henselian (its local ring is henselian and its residue field is separably closed), of mixed characteristic, with $\ell$ invertible. Here henselian means simple roots of monic polynomials over the residue field lift to $R$. Let $p_T:T\to S$ be an integral regular finite-type quasi-projective scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Quasi-projective means admitting a locally closed immersion into some $\mathbf P^N_S$. A regular closed immersion has ideal locally generated by a regular sequence [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. The virtual relative dimension $e_T$ of $p_T$ is $r-c$ in a local factorization as a regular closed immersion of codimension $c$ followed by a smooth morphism of relative dimension $r$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Put $K_T=p_T^!A_S(-e_T)[-2e_T]$.

The integer $e_T$ is well defined and constant. Every $S$-morphism $f:T\to U$ between such schemes is smoothable local complete intersection, with virtual dimension $e_f=e_T-e_U$. There is a canonical Kummer-normalized class
$$g_f:A_T(e_f)[2e_f]\longrightarrow f^!A_U.$$
For a regular closed immersion this is the class of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus], with its twist-shift moved to the source; for smooth $f$ it is the diagonal-class orientation of [lem-per-ordinary-smooth-orientation]. These classes are independent of the chosen smooth/regular factorization, commute with open restriction, and satisfy
$$g_{hf}=f^!(g_h)\circ g_f(e_h)[2e_h]$$
for composable morphisms, using exceptional transitivity and twist identifications. Write $c_T:A_T\to K_T$ for the normalized $g_{p_T}$. If $f$ is dominant and generically finite etale, then $e_f=0$, and transitivity identifies $f^!K_U$ with $K_T$ and gives $c_T=f^!(c_U)\circ g_f$. No assertion that $g_f$ or $c_T$ is an isomorphism is made.

source.place: Expose XVI, Definitions 2.5.1--2.5.3, Theorem 2.5.5, Definition 2.5.11 and Theorem 2.5.12; first paragraph of Proposition 3.5.7 proof, printed pp.249--250. Smooth class normalized by the existing diagonal/DNC orientation lem-per-ordinary-smooth-orientation.

proof.text: First supply global geometric factorizations. The trait is regular: at its closed point its dimension-one maximal ideal has one generator, and its generic local ring is a field. Every scheme in the statement is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Write a quasi-projective immersion as $T\hookrightarrow V\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_S$, the first map closed and the second open, using the definition of immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The standard projective charts [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-twisting-sheaf-charts], base changed by [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], are affine $N$-spaces. Thus [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth, lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-on-source, lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes] show $V\to S$ smooth of dimension $N$. Projective space is separated by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper], so $V\to S$ is separated: the diagonal restricts to a closed subscheme on any source open. The same argument makes $U\to S$ separated, and its base-changed diagonal makes $P\to V$ separated below. For an $S$-map $f:T\to U$, put $P=V\times_SU$. The map $(i,f):T\to P$ has closed composite $i$ with the separated projection $P\to V$; it is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-from-composite]. The projection $P\to U$ is smooth by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence], and $P$ is regular by [lem-per-regular-lci-geometric-calculus]. Hence $(i,f)$ is regular by that same node. This is a global regular-closed/smooth factorization of $f$.

The pointwise formula in [lem-per-regular-lci-geometric-calculus] gives, for a factorization of $f:T\to U$ and $t\mapsto u$, $e_f=\dim\mathcal O_{T,t}-\dim\mathcal O_{U,u}+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(u)}\kappa(t)$. It applies on arbitrary regular Noetherian schemes, not only the affine existence clause of that node. It proves factorization independence and local constancy of $e_f$. In particular $e_T$ is constant since $T$ is integral and therefore connected [def-pc-integral-scheme]. For $s=p_T(t)=p_U(u)$, subtract the formulas for $p_T$ and $p_U$ and use [lem-sbc-transcendence-degree-tower] for $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(u)\to\kappa(t)$: the result is $e_f=e_T-e_U$. The same subtraction for three schemes gives $e_{hf}=e_f+e_h$. If $f$ is dominant generically finite etale, take their generic points: both local rings are fields, and their finite residue extension has transcendence degree zero, so $e_f=0$.

source.place: Definitions 2.5.1--2.5.3; first paragraph of Proposition 3.5.7 proof

proof.text: All maps just constructed are separated and finite type over Noetherian schemes, hence compactifiable by [thm-nagata-compactification]. Use the ordinary compact-support right adjoints [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. These right adjoints live on the unbounded ordinary categories, so the composition comparison $Rh_!Rf_!\simeq R(hf)_!$ is taken there, from [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons]; on bounded-below inputs it restricts to that of [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons]. With [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition] this gives $(hf)^!\simeq f^!h^!$, with pasted counits. Put $a^?=a^!(-e_a)[-2e_a]$. The signed Tate lines and their inverse-image identifications are those of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. For clarity the exceptional twist identification follows by adjunction: for an invertible line $L$ on the target, move $a^*L$ across Hom using its inverse, apply $Ra_!\dashv a^!$, and move $L$ back. The projection formula needed in this Hom chain follows on a compactification from [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection] and the degreewise open-extension tensor identity (extension by zero has stalk either the given stalk or zero). Thus $a^!(M\otimes L)\simeq a^!M\otimes a^*L$. Together with Step 2 this gives $f^?h^?\simeq(hf)^?$. All these comparisons use pasted adjunctions; their associativity follows by taking the three Hom adjunctions in succession. Write $b\star a=u^?(b)\circ a$ for a class $a$ on $u$ and a class $b$ on the next map. Then $\star$ is associative.

For a factorization $f=pi$, put $a_i:A_T\to i^?A_P$ equal to the $n=1$ supported Kummer class of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus], and $a_p:A_P\to p^?A_U$ equal to the shifted diagonal/DNC orientation of [lem-per-ordinary-smooth-orientation]. Define $a_{p,i}=a_p\star a_i$. This is a global morphism $A_T\to f^?A_U$, since Step 1 provided a global factorization. Moving the twist-shift to the source gives $g_{p,i}:A_T(e_f)[2e_f]\to f^!A_U$. The two mixed identities [lem-per-smooth-gysin-mixed-identities], specialized to $n=1$, apply to exactly these maps: its prime-power smooth orientation at $n=1$ is the same diagonal/DNC orientation, by the construction and normalization clauses of [lem-per-noetherian-prime-power-smooth-duality, lem-per-ordinary-smooth-orientation]. No immersion class is inverted in this construction.

source.place: Definition 2.5.4; Lemmas 2.5.7--2.5.8, using the existing diagonal/DNC versions of their mixed identities

proof.text:
Compare factorizations with $i=qi'$ and $p'=pq$, where $q:P'\to P$ is smooth and separated. Form $X'=T\times_PP'$ with projections $j:X'\hookrightarrow P'$ and $q':X'\to T$, and section $s:T\to X'$ induced by $i'$. The geometric node [lem-per-regular-lci-geometric-calculus] makes $j$ regular (smooth maps are flat by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]) and $s$ regular, with $js=i'$. The mixed identities of [lem-per-smooth-gysin-mixed-identities] give $a_{q'}\star a_s=1$ and $a_q\star a_j=a_i\star a_{q'}$. Immersion composition [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] now yields
$$a_i=a_i\star a_{q'}\star a_s=a_q\star a_j\star a_s=a_q\star a_{i'}.$$
Smooth composition [lem-per-ordinary-smooth-orientation] gives $a_{p'}=a_p\star a_q$, hence $a_{p,i}=a_{p',i'}$. This is an equality of the specified morphisms, so it proves independence in the dominated case.

source.place: Theorem 2.5.5 proof, dominated-factorization diagram and the three displayed equalities

proof.text: For arbitrary global factorizations $T\xrightarrow iP\xrightarrow pU$ and $T\xrightarrow{i'}P'\xrightarrow{p'}U$, take $W=P\times_UP'$. Both projections are smooth by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence], and $W$ is regular by [lem-per-regular-lci-geometric-calculus]. The map $k=(i,i'):T\to W$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-from-composite], applied to the separated projection $W\to P$ and its closed composite $i$; it is regular by [lem-per-regular-lci-geometric-calculus]. Thus $k$ followed by $W\to U$ is a global factorization dominating both given ones. Step 5 compares it with each. Consequently $a_f$ and $g_f$ are independent of all global smooth/regular choices. A local factorization computes the restriction of this same class by applying this comparison after restricting the global factorization; no gluing of morphisms in a derived category is required.

source.place: Theorem 2.5.5 proof, reduction by the fibre product of the two smooth ambient schemes

proof.text: An identity immersion has Kummer class $1$, including codimension zero, by [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus]. The identity smooth orientation is the dimension-zero etale comparison by [lem-per-ordinary-smooth-orientation]. Choosing one of these identity factors shows that $g_f$ specializes to the stated immersion class or smooth orientation. Both factor classes commute with open restriction by these same nodes. The exceptional restriction identification is [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality] for a source open, and [lem-amb-shriek-open-exchange-adjoint] for a target open. Restricting the defining composite therefore gives the composite of the restricted factors; Step 6 identifies it with the already constructed restricted class. Kummer signs agree because the immersion factors are the supported Kummer classes and the smooth factors have the diagonal/DNC normalization throughout.

source.place: Definition 2.5.11; open restriction in Definitions 2.3.1 and 2.5.4

proof.text: For composition $T\xrightarrow fU\xrightarrow hZ$, choose $U\xrightarrow jQ\xrightarrow qZ$ with $j$ regular closed and $q$ smooth. Choose an immersion $T\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_S$ as in Step 1. The closed graph on the open ambient of Step 1 gives an immersion $T\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_U$. Choose an open $V\subseteq\mathbf P^N_U$ in which $T$ is closed. Since $\mathbf P^N_U$ is closed in $\mathbf P^N_Q$, this open is the inverse image of an open $W\subseteq\mathbf P^N_Q$; this is the definition of the subspace topology for a closed immersion. Let $i:T\hookrightarrow V$, $j':V\hookrightarrow W$, $p:V\to U$ and $p':W\to Q$. The standard charts and smooth restriction of Step 1 show $p,p'$ smooth, and the square with $j,j'$ is Cartesian. The geometric node [lem-per-regular-lci-geometric-calculus] makes $j'$ regular by flat base change, $i$ regular since its ambient scheme is smooth over regular $U$, and $j'i$ regular by composition. Thus $T\xrightarrow{j'i}W\xrightarrow{qp'}Z$ is a permitted factorization of $hf$.

source.place: Theorem 2.5.12 proof, projective-ambient diagram; use an ambient open so both immersion factors are closed

proof.text:
Using the factorization of Step 8, immersion composition [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus], smooth composition [lem-per-ordinary-smooth-orientation], and the Cartesian mixed identity [lem-per-smooth-gysin-mixed-identities] give
$$a_{hf}=(a_q\star a_{p'})\star(a_{j'}\star a_i)=a_q\star(a_j\star a_p)\star a_i=(a_q\star a_j)\star(a_p\star a_i)=a_h\star a_f.$$
Here the middle equality uses $a_{p'}\star a_{j'}=a_j\star a_p$, with the regular immersion $j$ and smooth map $p'$. Step 6 allows these particular factorizations. Since $e_{hf}=e_f+e_h$, moving the twist-shifts to the source gives precisely $g_{hf}=f^!(g_h)\circ g_f(e_h)[2e_h]$.

source.place: Theorem 2.5.12 proof, its last three displayed equalities

proof.text: Apply the construction to $p_T$ to obtain $c_T=a_{p_T}:A_T\to K_T$. For any $f:T\to U$, Step 2 and the pasted transitivity of Step 3 identify $f^?K_U=K_T$ and Step 9 gives $c_T=f^?(c_U)\circ a_f$. If $f$ is dominant generically finite etale, $e_f=0$, so $f^?=f^!$ and $a_f=g_f$. The result is $f^!K_U\simeq K_T$ and $c_T=f^!(c_U)\circ g_f$, as claimed. These identities only use the classes, not absolute-purity isomorphisms. In particular a scheme supported on the closed point is allowed: at its generic point the Step 2 formula is $e_T=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(\eta_T)-1$, so for $T=s$ it gives $e_T=-1$, not zero.

The statement is byte-identical to the Q41 base, so nothing is weakened. Removing the proper-morphism stmt_dep and adding lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback (it defines the negative twists) is correct. No new nodes, no cycles, no SGA. Checks by step: Step 1, the global P=V×_SU factorization (closed-from-composite with a separated V-projection, regular ambient). Step 2, the dimension formula, which gives e_f=e_T−e_U, e=−1 at the closed point and e_f=0 at generic points. Steps 5–6 match ILO 2.5.5: the section identity, the Cartesian mixed identity and immersion composition give a_i=a_q⋆a_{i'}, and W=P×_UP' dominates both factorizations. Step 4: at n=1 the prime-power orientation is the same three-factor DNC construction as lem-per-ordinary-smooth-orientation. Steps 8–9 match the ILO 2.5.12 diagram (V=W×_QU is Cartesian); I re-derived the twist bookkeeping for g_{hf}=f^!(g_h)∘g_f(e_h)[2e_h]. Step 10 is elementary. One fault, C4 in Step 3: f^! is the right adjoint on the unbounded categories, but lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons gives Rh_!Rf_!≅R(hf)_! only on D^+. The fix adds lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons (to the step, proof_deps and tool_uses); that comparison restricts on bounded-below inputs to the D^+ one. Duplicate check: the regular/prime-power/absolute Gysin nodes assume affine excellent schemes and assert isomorphisms, so none is a duplicate. The flagged trf/pod nodes are generic tools, not steps of the trace-formula or Poincaré-duality proofs: lisse-module algebra, affine translation trace, the regular-sequence dimension formula and DNC section deformation.
